findings.title: two_zone_mode 'auto' (the default) forces the two-zone model on every one-zone install, ignoring its heat-loss figure
findings.claim: On every install that configures no lower-floor sensor, no zone key and no explicit two_zone_mode, ThermalParameters.from_config enables the two-zone model, so the coordinator plans a lower zone the config never gave it and plans the same energy whatever single-zone heat-loss figure the user entered (20.511 kWh at 0.10 and at 0.30 kW/K).
findings.mechanism: thermal_model.ThermalParameters.from_config: `if two_zone_mode in (const.TWO_ZONE_MODE_ON, const.DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE): two_zone_enabled = True`. DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE is 'auto', and a missing key also defaults to 'auto', so 'auto' is treated as 'on'. The presence rule the comment above it says 'auto' means sits in the else-branch, which only an unknown value can now reach. With two zones on, the options flow hides house_heat_loss_coefficient (it is gated `_single_zone`), and the model uses the upper/lower defaults 0.08 + 0.07 = 0.15 kW/K. The setup diagram (describe_setup) and the card's setup page then draw a 'Lower floor' box (2 on the minimal plant).

findings.title: Scalar flow_lift_factor is inverted: lifting water hotter RAISES COP (up to 2.02x), breaking batch parity
findings.claim: ThermalModel.flow_lift_factor returns max(0.25, carnot_ref/carnot_flow), which is >1 for every flow above the 35 degC reference, so compute_cop (valve plant, direct-plant curve) and compute_cop_dhw rise with flow/tank temperature on every climate, while the batch twin _batch_cop applies carnot_flow/carnot_ref.
findings.mechanism: The ratio of two Carnot COPs is inverted in the scalar law only. carnot_flow < carnot_ref above the reference, so ref/flow > 1: a 55 degC hot-water charge is priced at 1.34-1.61x the space COP instead of 0.62-0.75x, a throttled buffer at the tank temperature likewise, and the Carnot fraction of the priced COP exceeds 1 (a COP above the Carnot limit) on 21320 grid points in four of five climates. _batch_cop uses carnot_flow/carnot_ref, so scalar and batch disagree by up to 8.01 COP units on the same inputs.

findings.title: Measured defrost derate never derates: derate_from_duty adds duty x 1.5 and clamps to 1.0
findings.claim: defrost.derate_from_duty returns min(1, max(0.55, 1 + duty*1.5)) instead of the module's documented 1 - duty*DEFROST_LOSS_MULTIPLIER, so every measured duty in (0, 0.30] yields 1.0 and a fully trusted 20 % defrost duty leaves the frost-band COP unchanged (ratio 1.0, documented 0.70).

findings.title: CoordinatorContext is not write-once: two in-place _opt_config writers reach every superseded context
findings.claim: After async_update_thermal_params supersedes a context, async_set_target_temperature and _apply_comfort_weight still change 2 fields (target_temp, comfort_weight) of the superseded context, because every published context shares one mutable OptimizationConfig; replacing the two writes by a published replace() leaves 0.
findings.mechanism: CoordinatorContext is a frozen dataclass whose docstring promises 'a change is published whole by rebinding _ctx ... a holder of the old one keeps a consistent view'. publish/_publish_params/async_update_thermal_params honour it for _current_state, _thermal_params and _config (the old holder keeps heat_loss_coefficient 0.15 while the live one reads 0.2), but coordinator.py:4258 (ctx._opt_config.target_temp = temperature) and :10941 (_opt_config.comfort_weight = ...) edit the member in place, and dataclasses.replace copies the member reference, so every context ever published since the entry was set up sees the edit. Today's holders across an await (enum_m4.py ctx_held: 8 sites) only read; no measured wrong value follows, hence low.

evidence.unit: fields of a superseded context's members changed after supersession
evidence.machine: box B5, round-11 finder container, CPython 3.14, numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1

perturbation.change: --perturb-ctx: both writers publish self._ctx = replace(ctx, _opt_config=replace(ctx._opt_config, <field>=...)) instead of the in-place assignment

findings.metric_definition: Number of fields of _opt_config/_thermal_params/_current_state on a captured context whose value changes after a later publish superseded that context.
findings.phenomenon_property: No production statement assigns into a field of a CoordinatorContext member; every change to a hub is a new published context, so a superseded context never changes.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py: the two _opt_config writers publish a replaced config (or OptimizationConfig becomes frozen behind the _hub facade)
